item.title: Houston Astros add pitcher Jackson Nezuh to 40-man roster to protect him from possible Rule 5 draft
item.description: The Astros have added right-hander Jackson Nezuh, who split 2026 between Double-A Corpus Christi and Triple-A Sugar Land, to their 40-man roster. (JoMando Cruz/MLB Photos via Getty Images) The Houston Astros selected pitching prospect Jackson Nezuh to their 40-man roster Tuesday, protecting the right-hander from Rule 5 draft eligibility. Whether this year's Rule 5 draft will even happen is unclear. The Rule 5 draft is scheduled for December at the winter meetings, which could be cancelled if baseball enters a lockout when the collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1. If that happens, it is uncertain if the Rule 5 draft would be postponed or cancelled. When the sport last endured a lockout during the 2021-22 offseason, the Rule 5 draft was not rescheduled after the lockout lifted in early March. Clubs are not permitted to contact or make transactions involving players on 40-man rosters during a lockout. So, for Nezuh, addition to the 40-man comes with the possibility of being among the players locked out on Dec. 1. THE NEW GM: How Randy Flores views roster, trades and offseason Nezuh, 24, was drafted by the Astros in the 14th round in 2023 out of Louisiana-Lafayette. He was rated the No. 16 overall prospect in their minor-league system by Baseball America and MLB Pipeline in those outlets' latest rankings. Nezuh has started 52 of 73 outings in the Astros' system, posting a 3.99 ERA, a .224 opponents' batting average and a 2.8-to-1 strikeout-to-walk ratio. He had a 3.97 ERA in 65 2/3 innings at Double-A Corpus Christi this season before a promotion to Triple-A, where he posted a 3.58 ERA in 37 2/3 innings. Among the Rule 5-eligible pitchers the Astros did not protect Tuesday - the deadline to add them to the 40-man roster - were right-handers James Hicks, Hudson Leach and Alonzo Tredwell. All were ranked among their top 30 prospects by Baseball America. Prospects are eligible for the Rule 5 draft after four professional seasons if they were drafted or signed at age 19 or older, and after five seasons if drafted or signed at 18 or younger. Nezuh's addition left Houston with 39 players on its 40-man roster as of Tuesday afternoon. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Lane Kiffin Admits Nightmares After Texas Loss To Arch Manning
item.description: LSU head coach Lane Kiffin answers questions during a press conference after a college football game between Ole Miss and LSU at Vaught Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, Miss., on Saturday, Sept. 19, 2026. Ole Miss defeated LSU 32-24. Lane Kiffin is not sleeping well after the Texas loss, and he admits it openly. The LSU head coach told reporters on Monday that he wakes up every hour with a nightmare about the final play. He said, “I wake up literally every hour the last two nights, and I have this nightmare of the last play of the game.” That level of raw honesty is rare for a coach who usually spins bad news into good stories. Many fans want to tear him apart for a 6-4 start in Year 1, but the numbers show a team that fought hard. The Tigers outgained Texas 366-273 and held a 21-10 lead in the third quarter before collapsing late. Kiffin knows this record looks bad on paper, yet he insists the program is moving forward. “Obviously, it’s really important for the right now and the feeling right now and what we want to give to our fans and what we want our older players to experience, we’re not winning enough,” Kiffin said. The Nightmare of One Play The loss to Texas came down to a single defensive breakdown that still haunts the coach. Raleek Brown scored on a four-yard touchdown pass from Arch Manning with just three seconds left on the clock. Kiffin blamed his team for failing to cover the receiver in that crucial moment. He admitted, “We’re not gonna f cover the guy, and he’s gonna walk in the f (end zone).” That mistake cost LSU the game and any realistic hope for the College Football Playoff. According to EssentiallySports , Kiffin continues to suffer nightmares regarding the Texas loss, indicating the heavy burden this defeat places on him. He described seeing the play over and over again in his sleep, including his own failed attempt to call a timeout. The coach said, “Then I wake up, and it’s real. Then I go back to sleep for an hour, and I wake up, and it’s real again.” This is not a coach hiding behind excuses; he is staring directly at the mistake that ended his season. A Tough Year for a Big Brand Kiffin entered this job with a massive reputation, but the results so far do not match the hype. Passing on the opportunity to coach Ole Miss during last year’s postseason, he instead managed a Year 1 flop in Baton Rouge costing $100 million. Every LSU discussion leading up to next year’s SEC media days will focus on his struggles to beat ranked teams. “This season has been so much,” Kiffin said at his Monday news conference. “Just a lot.” Despite the poor record, the path to a different narrative was there if the team had won a few more close games. item.description: Cameron Smith tees off on 5 of the Players Stadium Course Monday, March 14, 2022 at TPC Sawgrass in Ponte Vedra Beach. Monday marked finishing third rounds and final rounds of golf for The Players Championship. Cameron Smith from Australia and resident of Jacksonville won the event at -13 par. Cameron Smith and Bryson DeChambeau have signed deals to play on the DP World Tour after LIV Golf ceased operations. Australian Golf Digest reports Smith accepted invites to a specific number of tournaments, while DeChambeau secured Category 1 status for the 2027 season. This shift brings eighteen former LIV players back to the European circuit, including major winners Dustin Johnson and Bubba Watson. The tour confirmed these moves on Tuesday as the breakaway league announced it would wind down operations. DeChambeau holds the top priority ranking on the new list. This status allows the American to choose which tournaments he plays without restriction. The 33-year-old two-time major champion already has a confirmed spot at the Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa starting December 4. The two Australian tournaments kicking off the tour season in late November will not feature his participation. DeChambeau chose the Nedbank event over the Australian PGA Championship at The Lakes in Sydney. Invites Managed to Protect Current Members The European Tour faces pressure to balance star power with member rights. Guy Kinnings, CEO of the tour, stated the decision to offer invites had to be “carefully managed” by the circuit. He added that the process aims “to ensure and preserve playing opportunities for existing members.” Nine former LIV players signed agreements for limited invites rather than full membership. These spots exclude the high-profile Rolex Series events but target smaller tournaments where their presence adds value. After securing victories in the final two contests of the 2026 European season, former world No. 1 Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton are back on the tour. They announced their return alongside the nine players on invite deals. Lee Westwood, Sergio Garcia, Henrik Stenson, and Ian Poulter also join the roster via a category based on career earnings. Over the last 12 months, the tour observed substantial shifts within the men’s professional golf landscape. On Monday, PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp stated that his board held “thoughtful discussions” regarding the future of players at LIV Golf. He added: “I hope to have more to say in the beginning of the new year.” This comment suggests a return to the PGA Tour remains blocked by the one-year ban rule for players with recent LIV appearances. item.description: The San Antonio Gunslingers will host open tryouts Nov. 21, giving local athletes a chance to earn a spot on the professional indoor football team's 2027 roster. (Marvin Pfeiffer/San Antonio Express-News) The San Antonio Gunslingers are looking for their next wave of talent, giving local football players a chance to prove they belong on the field. The professional indoor football team will hold open tryouts for its 2027 Indoor Football League season Saturday, Nov. 21, at the Gunslingers' practice facility, 9450 NE Loop 410. Tryouts will run from 10 a.m. to noon, with registration and check-in beginning at 9 a.m. Participation costs $60. Athletes must bring turf shoes; cleats are not permitted. The Gunslingers' coaching staff will evaluate players. The staff is led by new head coach Billy Back, who was hired Sept. 5. Back is a five-time championship-winning coach. Before joining San Antonio, he led the Frisco Fighters to the league's best regular-season record in back-to-back seasons. "We are looking for guys who are tough, competitive, and coachable," Back said in a news release. "We want players who bring energy, play with a purpose, and are willing to do whatever it takes to help build the new foundation of this team." item.title: Charles Leclerc launches pop-up café at Wynn Las Vegas for race week
item.description: Motorsport photo The 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix is officially taking over the Strip, and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc is extending his brand well beyond the paddock. As teams prepare for the massive 1.9-kilometre straight down Las Vegas Boulevard, Leclerc is launching a highly publicised off-track venture for his fans. According to a promotional Instagram post from the @lasbucketlist account, the Ferrari star is bringing his own dedicated pop-up café to Wynn Las Vegas. Dubbed "Café Leclerc", the activation completely takes over Wynn's existing Caffé Al Teatro. The limited-time experience runs throughout race week, opening on Wednesday, 18 November, and closing on Sunday, 22 November. What is on the menu? The Las Vegas Grand Prix is notorious for its sky-high VIP hospitality prices, but Café Leclerc is designed to be a highly accessible fan experience. According to the social media announcement, the Café will operate on a standard walk-up basis with absolutely no reservations required. Fans visiting the Wynn activation can expect a curated menu featuring speciality drinks and pastries, alongside a selection of exclusive merchandise only available during the race weekend. View this post on Instagram While the Café bears his name, it is important to note that an official in-person appearance by Leclerc at Caffé Al Teatro has not been formally announced. Fans hoping to catch a glimpse of the Monegasque driver off-track will have better luck at the PUMA Flagship store, where he is scheduled to join Lewis Hamilton for the "Under the Lights" event on Tuesday evening. A hub for driver brands Wynn Las Vegas is heavily leaning into individual driver brands for the 2026 event. In addition to Café Leclerc, the resort is also hosting a dedicated retail pop-up for Hamilton's +44 streetwear clothing brand, located in the Encore Esplanade during the same 18 November–22 window. item.title: Red Sox Can Make Ketel Marte Trade and Have Franklin Arias on Roster
item.description: Red Sox Can Make Ketel Marte Trade and Have Franklin Arias on Roster originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Red Sox need to get better this offseason, and few players can help them more than Ketel Marte of the Arizona Diamondbacks. Marte, who has been in trade rumors over the past year and a half, is one of the better players in Major League Baseball. Unfortunately, there do seem to be some problems off the field out in Arizona, though that could benefit the Red Sox. While Boston makes sense as a suitor because it has to improve on both sides of the baseball, specifically offensively, there could be some questions about whether it makes sense to bring him in because of Franklin Arias. However, there's still a situation in which the Red Sox can call up Arias, play Marte daily at second base, and have Trevor Story healthy and at his best. Bleacher Report, though, doesn't believe that's the case any longer. When recently examining landing spots for the All-Star second baseman, the outlet suggested that Marte was once a fit for the Red Sox, but no longer is. “The Red Sox were the hypothetical landing spot numero uno for Ketel Marte last offseason. Considering second base ended up being a completely underwhelming revolving door of Marcelo Mayer, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Anthony Siegler and Nick Sogard, they probably regret not doing more to make it happen,” Bleacher Report’s Kerry Miller wrote . “But now? After watching Franklin Arias blossom into one of the top prospects in all of baseball, trading for Curtis Mead at the 2026 deadline and already signing Jake Bauers this offseason? With a projected cash payroll already north of $209M, which is a mark they haven't had on Opening Day since 2022?” Some of those concerns are more than fair, but Marte doesn't necessarily make a ton of money. He's on a six-year, $105 million deal that goes through 2030. For a team like the Red Sox, that's not exactly the biggest concern. Since 2023, Marte has been one of the most productive players in baseball. He has 111 home runs, a 133 OPS+, and an .851 OPS. He's also posted an 18.5 bWAR in that span. item.title: Chargers End 11-Game Skid With First Win Over Ravens In Monday Night Upset
item.description: James Lang-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Chargers finally broke their losing streak on Monday night with a 23-20 victory over the Baltimore Ravens, according to the New York Post . This win ended an 11-game slide for Los Angeles and marked their first win of the 2026 season. The game also ended a combined 15-game losing streak for both teams entering the matchup, a record for a Monday Night Football contest. Justin Herbert led the charge with a 22-yard touchdown run, while the defense held Baltimore to just 16 rushing yards. Baltimore struggled mightily despite the debut of new quarterback Jacoby Brissett. The Ravens started the night by going three-and-out on their first three possessions, drawing loud boos from the home crowd. Brissett threw for 340 yards in his first game with Baltimore, but the offense could not find enough support. Derrick Henry, a key part of the plan, was held to just 10 yards on 10 carries even though he managed to score two touchdowns. The Ravens have now lost five straight games and seven of their last eight home contests. How The Chargers Won The Line Of Scrimmage The difference in the game came down to the ground attack. Los Angeles outrushed Baltimore by a massive margin of 160 yards to 16. Omarion Hampton was the star for the Chargers, carrying the ball 22 times for 105 yards. He scored on a 1-yard run late in the second quarter to help build a lead. The Chargers offense scored on their first possession when Herbert ran for a touchdown. This early score gave Los Angeles a lead they would not relinquish for the rest of the night. Justin Herbert played a clean game by avoiding mistakes. He threw 12 completions on 18 attempts for 129 yards while avoiding turnovers for the first time this season. The defense did its job by forcing two turnovers and holding the Ravens to 287 total yards. A critical moment came when Dalvin Tomlinson sacked Brissett. Later, Zay Flowers fumbled the ball near the Los Angeles 45-yard line, which sealed the game for the visitors. Baltimore’s Struggles Continue Despite New Quarterback The Ravens hoped the trade for Jacoby Brissett would stabilize their offense. item.description: Aggies Quarterback Marcel Reed 10, The LSU Tigers take on the Texas A&M Aggies. September 19, 2026; Baton Rouge, LA, USA; at Tiger Stadium. CBS Sports has made a clear call on Texas A&M’s future, stating the team will move on from senior quarterback Marcel Reed after the 2026 season. The prediction comes after a brutal 22-7 loss to No. 8 Tennessee on Saturday where the Aggies offense managed just 179 total yards. Reed threw for only 71 yards and an interception before Brady Hart replaced him as the backup and also threw a pick. The numbers show a program in deep trouble, sitting at 4-6 overall and 1-6 in SEC play. Why the Reed Experiment Failed The offense looks broken because the coaching staff refuses to adapt to what works on the field. Holmon Wiggins, the first-year offensive coordinator, has called a bland game with zero creativity that leaves Reed unable to make plays. In conference games, Reed recorded only two touchdowns and eight interceptions as the team had difficulty advancing the ball. Mike Elko’s loyalty to Wiggins and Reed has cost the team wins, and the fan base is losing patience with Year 3 of this same plan. The ship has sailed on Reed as the starter, according to CBS Sports analyst Brad Crawford, because the current pairing simply does not work. Teams in the SEC have figured out how to stop him, and the Aggies have no counter-plan. The Real Problem Is the Play-Caller Texas A&M has the money to land a top quarterback in the transfer portal, but the coaching staff might scare them away. Elko needs to decide if Holmon Wiggins stays as the play-caller before signing a new signal-caller. Reed’s success has come from scrambling and pulling the ball on zone reads, yet the team refuses to design runs for him. During a Monday press conference, Elko admitted the offense was never built around Reed as a runner, even though he thrives in the open field. “He pulls the ball on zone reads. That’s where he gets his runs. He scrambles. I just think teams are aware of that, and they’re not letting him do it.” This quote from Elko confirms the coaching staff knows the problem but chooses to ignore it. If Wiggins returns, top targets like Alabama’s Austin Mack or Virginia Tech’s Ethan Grunkemeyer will likely look elsewhere. A New Direction Is the Only Option The Aggies require a passer capable of sustaining drives on third down and punishing defenses, particularly in those situations. The current roster and scheme are stuck in the past while the rest of the SEC moves forward. Texas A&M has the resources to fix this, but only if Elko stops protecting underperforming staff members.

item.title: Wales' Nations League campaign boosts Bellamy's belief
item.description: Former Wales captain Craig Bellamy was appointed head coach in July 2024 [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Craig Bellamy kept coming back to one word. Belief. His Wales side had just lost a fifth game out of six to finish bottom of their Nations League group. Bellamy would have been forgiven for feeling a little bruised. But there are ways of losing and ways of finishing bottom. Wales were fearless against Portugal, exhilarating in attack and proving they can compete at the highest level of this competition, even as they were beaten 3-2 in Cardiff. And while they were already consigned to the foot of the Group A4 table, Wales' previous performances meant they at least had the back-up of a relegation play-off in March to preserve their top-flight status. "Belief's the biggest one," Bellamy said when he was asked what he and his team had taken from this campaign. "Not just this game, but in general. We are beyond close to this level. We can more than compete at this level. "We demand and want to expect to be. Getting into League A is big for us, but also staying in A is going to allow us to develop. "You can only develop and improve by playing the best teams, and I felt we've taken another shift." Portugal hold off bold Wales in five-goal thriller Wales have certainly fared better than they did when they were last in the top tier of the Nations League, when they finished with one point from six games and were relegated. Victory against World Cup quarter-finalists Norway last month was their first at this level and, had they been more clinical in Oslo on Saturday, they might have got a second win of the campaign. Ultimately, Wales' inability to take their chances, – combined with sloppy defensive mistakes – meant their results did not match their performances. And the reality is that they were up against stellar opposition, whose vastly superior resources showed with their greater ruthlessness at both ends of the pitch. "If there's anything you would have learned from these games, then you see killers. That's why they're at the top," Bellamy added. "I know people look at results. I'm fully aware of the business. This is all I know. But I think when you look at reality as well, and you look at our performances during this group, I couldn't ask for more. "I feel we're closer than probably maybe the players thought they were. It's fine margins. "But I feel the biggest word out of this now has been belief, really, for me." Las Vegas Raiders rookie Fernando Mendoza took the field for a big start on Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks , but he couldn't pull off a win. The Raiders fell in a 21-13 game, and it wasn't pretty. But don't be so quick to judge. It doesn't mean Mendoza isn't cut out to be the Raiders' franchise quarterback. At least, that's the take from one NFL analyst looking at the situation. Ben Solak of ESPN has released a list with his thoughts on what happened last weekend across the NFL and how it will impact things moving forward. For the Raiders, he stands up for Mendoza and his debut. ESPN analyst urges patience with Fernando Mendoza after Raiders debut Why should Mendoza be given the benefit of the doubt? Mendoza shouldn't be judged too harshly because he was missing Brock Bowers and working with a limited receiving corps. It's that simple. "If Mendoza were in his fourth or fifth start throwing to this group of receivers, we would know that the talent is insufficient to get a fair read on a budding passer," he notes in the piece. Solak adds, "I'm not interested in any sweeping Mendoza takeaways until he gets a normal game with a healthy Bowers." That's a strong statement. We know Mendoza would have a bit of a learning curve going from college to the pros. Having him without Bowers put him at a huge disadvantage. item.description: COLUMBUS, OHIO - JUNE 18, 2026: Kody Huff #6 of the Columbus Clippers in the field during the fourth inning against the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders at Huntington Park on June 18, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Guardians brought their roster to 40 tonight adding Justin Campbell, Kody Huff and Jaison Chourio to the roster to protect them from a potential Rule 5 draft. Campbell is a 6’5 LHP out of Oklahoma State, drafted with the 37th pick of the 2022 draft. Unfortunately, a variety of injuries kept him out of pitching in pro ball until last season when his story was one of the best to come out of the Guardians’ org. He had a 2.48/3.03 ERA/FIP with a 10.83/4.30 K/BB/9 between Akron and Columbus and pitched 69 innings (dealing with a lower body issue for a six-week session). Hopefully he has a healthy offseason and is able to pitch in Columbus and then Cleveland in 2027 when a new CBA is presumably put in place. Huff is a 25 year-old right-handed hitting catcher who got some time at third base and first base in Columbus last year. Acquired from Colorado in the Cal Quantrill trade, Huff had a bit of an offensive breakout last year, with a .264/.375/.513 slashline good for a 132 wRC+ and a 19.5/13.9 K/BB%. He benefited from hitting in the very friendly confines of Columbus but actually had a higher OPS on the road (.867/897 OPS) and hits LHP much better than RHP (.949/867 OPS), but he may immediately be the pairing for Patrick Bailey or get consideration to replace David Fry. He really only particularly struggled in Triple-A against offspeed: his numbers were great against fastballs and solid vs. Breaking balls. Finally, Chourio was added, indicating the Guardians suspect someone might try to stash the 21 year-old as a defensive specialist/pinch-runner for a season should a Rule 5 draft be held. Chourio, a switch-hitting outfielder signed in 2022 as the younger brother of Jackson Chourio, only had a 114 wRC+ between Lake County and Akron last season with a 20/14 K/BB%, but stole 42 bases in 51 attempts and played 64 of 113 games in centerfield. He’s been better, overall, hitting left-handed than right-handed but there is still reason for optimism he can be above average vs. LHP. item.description: Reinhold Matay-Imagn Images Edoardo Mortara set the fastest time for Mahindra on the opening day of Formula E testing at Jarama. The Swiss driver posted a lap of 1m24.344s, finishing three tenths ahead of Nissan’s Zane Maloney. This session marked the first collective run for the new Gen4 cars on the outskirts of Madrid. Motorsport.com reported the test began on Monday, November 16, 2026, signaling the start of a new technical era for the championship. The day faced significant delays with seven red flags total. Four stops happened in the morning and three occurred in the afternoon. Issues ranged from radio system failures to cars leaving the track. The afternoon session saw the first crashes of the Gen4 machinery. Theo Pourchaire hit the barriers at Turn 3, while Nyck de Vries crashed at Turn 9 near the end of the day. Gen4 Technical Shifts and Power Gains The new Gen4 car brings major changes to performance and handling. Power in qualifying mode will rise to 600kW, which equals around 815bhp. Aerodynamic downforce has more than doubled compared to previous generations. Teams also gain permanent four-wheel drive for better grip. Development focused heavily on aerodynamics and tire performance. Gaillardot noted the need to introduce new solutions with Bridgestone as the new supplier. The goal is to show how far an electric single-seater can go. The car was redesigned to meet specific targets set by the FIA. Two distinct aerodynamic packages exist for high and low downforce needs. The high-downforce front wing sits lower with a different angle. Openings located on both sides allow airflow to move from the inner section toward the outer section. Other teams faced similar issues during the afternoon. Lola and Fortescue Zero also experienced problems on track. Enzo Fittipaldi’s Lola stopped at the end of the pitlane, triggering a red flag. Despite the chaos, drivers managed to improve their times. Mortara set the fastest lap of the day in the afternoon session. His time was six tenths of a second faster than Jean-Eric Vergne’s morning benchmark. Nissan’s Zane Maloney moved up to second place after a strong afternoon. He finished the day with a lap of 1m24.681s. The Porsche Team made progress after keeping a low profile in the morning. Nico Muller finished third and reigning champion Pascal Wehrlein came in fourth. Maximilian Guenther rounded out the top five drivers for the day. item.title: Dustin Johnson, 8 other ex-LIV golfers sign DP World Tour deal as the 2027 golf world takes shape
item.description: Nine ex-LIV stars have a DP World Tour path in 2027 Getty Images Bryson DeChambeau is headed to the DP World Tour after LIV Golf’s collapse, but he isn’t the only big name from the now-defunct rebel league that will call the European circuit home in 2027. On Tuesday, the DP World Tour announced the membership for the 2027 season. DeChambeau took up membership through an exemption he earned for winning the 2024 U.S. Open. He will play out of Category 1, which means he can play in any tournament he wants. Nine other former LIV Golf members signed a deal with the DP World Tour to receive special tournament invitations next year. Dustin Johnson, Cameron Smith, Bubba Watson, Joaquin Niemann, Abraham Ancer, Carlos Ortiz, Thomas Pieters, Lucas Herbert and Michael La Sasso will not get exemptions into the big-money Rolex Series events. Instead, those nine players will receive invites to regular DP World Tour events in an attempt to boost the field strength and attention for those events. According to a release from the DP World Tour, the tournaments those nine players can play in have been “prescribed” by the tour for each player to add value to certain events. Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, Sergio Garcia and others had already declared their intention to play on the DP World Tour in 2027 after leaving LIV Golf as it entered Chapter 11 bankruptcy court. Ian Poulter, Lee Westwood, Graeme McDowell, Paul Casey, Louis Oosthuizen, Martin Kaymer, Charl Schwartzel, Branden Grace and Henrik Stenson will all play out of the career-money category next season. “For us, it’s the prospect of having incredible talent joining our tour, which already is laden with talent,” DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings told Sky Sports last week about having ex-LIV players join the tour. “What it does is it brings it [strength in fields] at the time of year when our dual members are off in the United States and that will help those [DP World Tour] tournaments at that time of year.” LIV Golf officially died two weeks ago when the league’s lawyers told a New Jersey bankruptcy court it was winding down operations and no longer planning to reboot as LIV 2.0. item.title: NASCAR Attendance Hits Low Point As Empty Seats Mount In 2026
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The 2026 NASCAR Cup Series season ended with a title win for Kyle Larson at Homestead-Miami, but the celebration was muted by empty seats. Fans who packed the stands in past years stayed home, leaving massive tracks looking half full. Crowds have dropped at some of its most famous venues. Two races stood out for their lack of fans. Bristol Motor Speedway held its Food City 500 on April 12 with only 70,000 people in the stands. That number fills a small stadium, but it left huge gaps at a track built for 146,000 spectators. The turnout was roughly 48% of capacity, a sharp drop from the sellout crowds Bristol used to see every spring. Empty Seats at Historic Tracks Indianapolis Motor Speedway faced the same problem during the Brickyard 400 on July 26. Speedway president Doug Boles told drivers that about 70,000 fans were expected, a number he noted was like a sold-out NFL game. At Indianapolis, that crowd looked tiny against the massive grandstands. The 500-mile race earlier in the year had sold out, making the lack of fans for the NASCAR race even more noticeable. The contrast between the two events shows that fans are not leaving the sport entirely, but they are choosing other races over the Cup Series. TV Ratings Hit New Lows The trouble on the track was matched by numbers on television. The entire 2026 season averaged 2.42 million viewers, which is down 2% from 2025 and sets a new all-time low for the series. The season finale at Homestead-Miami drew 2.47 million viewers, an 8% drop from the previous year’s finale at Phoenix. According to Awful Announcing , this season finale for the Cup Series set a record as the least-watched. Five races in 2026 failed to reach 1.5 million viewers, and every single one of them aired on the USA Network. Phoenix Raceway finished at the bottom with just 1.294 million viewers. Among the bottom five, only that event dropped under 1.4 million. The shift to cable channels seems to be hurting the sport’s ability to reach casual fans who still watch on broadcast TV. There were some bright spots in the data. Both USA Network and NBC saw growth as adults aged 35 to 49 increased 27% across the Chase. However, the overall trend remains negative. The sport secured higher rights fees, but the fragmentation of the audience across cable and streaming is making it hard to grow. David Berson, president of Skydance Sports, will meet NASCAR CEO Steve O’Donnell to discuss moving races from TNT Sports to the CBS broadcast network. A shift of this nature might offer a significant audience boost for part of the schedule. The Homestead-Miami championship race averaged 476,000 Adults 18-49, which was a 20% increase, but the total viewer count keeps falling.

item.title: Kyler Gordon’s Shoulder Worry Looms Over Bears Week 11
item.description: Matt Marton-Imagn Images On Tuesday, head coach Ben Johnson stated that cornerback Kyler Gordon has a shoulder injury restricting his participation. The slot corner missed practice on Monday after the bye week, and his status for Week 11 remains unclear. Johnson told reporters that the situation is day-to-day and his team will watch closely as the week moves forward. The uncertainty is significant because Gordon has been a key part of the defense since returning from the PUP list. The Injury Details Gordon hurt his left shoulder during the win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers back on Sunday, November 8. The injury most likely happened when he dove and hit the ground while covering a 58-yard pass to wide receiver Tez Johnson. Although he left the field briefly, he returned to finish the game against the Bucs. He has played in four straight games since his activation, but missed Monday practice, which the coaching staff noted. A to Z Sports reported that Johnson noted the player wasn’t out there yesterday, making it a day-by-day thing for the team right now. A Vague Outlook When asked about Gordon’s status, the head coach simply said, “We’ll see as the week goes along.” The official injury report will be released on Wednesday. Heavy.com noted that this lack of a ringing endorsement is not the best sign for a player who needs to be ready to go. The team needs to know if Gordon can handle the Saints offense or if they must rely on backups. The Bears will practice Tuesday, have a day off Wednesday, and the injury report that day will offer the first real estimate. Depth Behind the Starter If Gordon cannot play, rookie Malik Muhammad II is ready to step into the slot. After sitting out two games due to a toe injury, Muhammad was back at practice on Monday. He split time with Cam Lewis while Gordon was sidelined earlier in the season and did a nice job filling the role. The Bears lost a player who recorded four sacks and two forced fumbles in the past four games. The team hosts the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, November 22, at 1 p.m. ET at Soldier Field.
